analysis.text: The city library will reopen its east entrance on Monday.
Staff have moved the help desk, added clearer signs, and tested the new lift with volunteers.
Visitors can still borrow books while the final inspection is underway.
Our research group reviewed the first survey before publishing the results.
The samples were collected in three regions, and each participant received the same questions.
The report explains what the data can show and where further study is needed.
The new schedule gives every department enough time to review the proposal.
Managers will share their comments by Friday, after which the project team can prepare a revised version.
No decision has been made about the launch date.
The results was shared with the committee yesterday, but nobody have checked the figures yet.
She don't expect the revised draft to arrive before the end of the week, although the editor could of sent it earlier.
Several customers asked for informations about the return policy.
The clerk explained that a receipt is required, and that opened items may be returned within thirty days.
Each request are reviewed by a supervisor before a refund is issued.
Before the team publishes its conclusion, it should recieve the final tables and check that the totals are consistent.
The analyst will compare the figures seperately, then send a short summary to everyone who needs it.
The meeting starts at 9:30 a.m. in Room 14.
Please bring the signed form, a copy of the agenda, and any questions you would like the chair to address.
The building is closed to visitors after 6 p.m.
We are looking forward to hear from the reviewers.
If they suggest a change, the author can update the draft and circulate it again.
The revised copy should be sent to Maria and I before it is approved.

matches.message: The pronoun 'She' is usually used with a third-person or a past tense verb.
It's never correct to use 'of' after a modal verb. Use <suggestion>could have</suggestion>, or, in informal register, <suggestion>could've</suggestion>.
The word 'informations' is a legal term. In standard English, the word 'information' is a non-count noun.
In the grammatical structure 'look + forward + to + verb', the verb 'to' is used with the gerund.
In this context, it seems that the correct pronoun is <suggestion>me</suggestion>.
